route.title: Dated return exhortation and remembered response
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The date and word-event formula at 1:1 introduces the return command, ancestral counterexample, rhetorical questions, and remembered admission; a WLC-family samekh follows 1:6 before the fresh night-vision date.
route.rationale: The unit moves from divine displeasure through the reciprocal return summons and ancestral warning to the reported recognition that the announced words overtook the ancestors.
route.counterevidence: The dated superscription is formally recoverable, but the saying introduction is syntactically incomplete without the exhortation it frames.

route.title: Night patrol, intercession, and commissioned comfort proclamation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A new date and word-event at 1:7 opens the night vision; patrol report, angelic intercession, comforting answer, and the command to proclaim continue to the paragraph closure after 1:17.
route.rationale: The patrol's report of an undisturbed earth creates the intercession answered by the restoration proclamation, so description, dialogue, and embedded oracle form one vision-report sequence.
route.counterevidence: The proclamation command at 1:14 is a genuine internal speech-form turn and could be indexed as a dependent child, but it answers the unresolved intercession rather than starting a new vision.

route.title: Four horns and four craftsmen
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The lifted-eyes formula at 1:18 introduces four horns after the prior vision closes; two questions and the craftsmen interpretation reach completion at 1:21 before another lifted-eyes object at 2:1.
route.rationale: The horns' scattering function and the craftsmen's counteraction are paired halves of one compact object vision and cannot be represented by separating the first question from the second.
route.counterevidence: WEB 1:18-21 corresponds to MT/WLC 2:1-4, and a WLC-family paragraph mark occurs internally after MT 2:2; numbering and layout corroborate but do not dictate the surface.

route.title: Measuring-line vision and unwalled Jerusalem promise
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The lifted-eyes formula and new measuring-line object at 2:1 open a vision; destination question, angelic relay, unwalled-city message, and wall-of-fire and indwelling-glory promise conclude before the doubled escape imperative at 2:6.
route.rationale: The measuring action is interpreted by the relay speech through 2:5, while the vocative flight command at 2:6 changes address, mood, and rhetorical form.
route.counterevidence: The glory promise at 2:5 also supplies the conceptual bridge to the dwelling promise in 2:10-11, so the split requires mandatory hydration to the whole 2:1-13 movement.

route.title: Escape summons and Zion indwelling song-proclamation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The doubled Come and flee command at 2:6-7 restarts with direct address; reversal against plundering nations, Zion's song command, indwelling, inheritance, and the all-flesh silence close at 2:13.
route.rationale: Flight from the north develops into the reason for rejoicing and silence: hostile nations are reversed, Yahweh dwells among joined peoples, and the movement closes with universal hush.
route.counterevidence: Speaker and pronoun pressure in 2:8-9 and paragraph marks after WEB 2:7 and 2:9 expose internal turns, but selecting a speaker or witness is unnecessary for the larger proclamation's form.

route.title: Joshua courtroom cleansing, charge, and sign oracle
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The showing formula at 3:1 opens one courtroom scene; rebuke, garment removal, investiture, solemn charge, sign interpretation, stone image, one-day removal, and in-that-day close remain within the same staged encounter.
route.rationale: Cleansing establishes the addressee and symbolic status required by the conditional charge and subsequent sign oracle, while 3:10 supplies the scene's peace image and closure.
route.counterevidence: The solemn assurance at 3:6 is a strong internal speech turn, and the speaker issue in 3:5 remains text-sensitive, but neither requires splitting the still-open courtroom scene.

route.title: Lampstand and olive trees interpreting dialogue
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The waking and seeing exchange at 4:1-3 introduces one lampstand-and-olive configuration; repeated questions, embedded words concerning Zerubbabel, and the resumed olive-tree questions culminate in the answer at 4:14.
route.rationale: The embedded words at 4:6-10 interpret aspects of the still-visible tableau and are followed by renewed questions about the same olive objects, making the full vision the safest surface.
route.counterevidence: The renewed word-event at 4:8 and WLC-family pe after 4:7 are real internal seams, and lamp or channel numerals remain translation-sensitive, but presentation as independent oracles would obscure the resumed interpreting dialogue.

route.title: Flying scroll and house-consuming curse
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The lifted-eyes formula and new flying-scroll object at 5:1 begin a vision; dimensions, curse interpretation, and its entry into offending houses complete at 5:4 before the interpreting angel comes forward with a different object.
route.rationale: Scroll description and curse effect are one question-interpretation unit whose causal and spatial outcome reaches closure at the destruction of timber and stones.
route.counterevidence: The curse declaration at 5:3 is an explanatory turn that could be separately cited, but detaching it would sever interpretation from the object whose meaning it supplies.

route.title: Ephah, Wickedness, and transport to Shinar
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The angel's forward movement and lift-your-eyes command at 5:5 introduce the ephah; identification, containment, winged transport, destination question, and emplacement answer continue through 5:11 and its paragraph close.
route.rationale: Although the vision changes action after Wickedness is sealed, the same ephah remains the object from appearance through removal and destination, so both phases belong together.
route.counterevidence: A WLC-family samekh after 5:8 marks an internal phase boundary, and the eye or iniquity wording at 5:6 is text-sensitive, but neither creates a new object vision at 5:9.

route.title: Four chariots dispatched through the earth
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Again I lifted my eyes at 6:1 introduces four chariots; horse catalogue, interpreting question, directional dispatch, permission to range, and the called-out north-country result conclude at 6:8 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: The final report that the northbound agents quieted the speaker's spirit resolves the interpretation and dispatch, while the renewed word-event at 6:9 clearly begins a sign-act.
route.counterevidence: The command at 6:7 is an action shift after the directional explanation, but it completes rather than replaces the chariot interpretation.

route.title: Crowning sign-act, interpretation, and memorial
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A renewed word-event at 6:9 commands same-day collection and crown making; crowning, addressed interpretation, temple-building declaration, memorial disposition, and conditional obedience close continue through 6:15 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: The physical act and its explanation depend on one another, and the crown's memorial placement and conditional close finish the commissioned sign-event.
route.counterevidence: Names, crown number, pronouns, and throne language are textual and interpretive hot zones, but those difficulties do not justify detaching the explanation from the enacted crown.

route.title: Dated fasting inquiry
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A new royal-year and month-day frame at 7:1 opens the event; the Bethel delegation's favor-seeking and question to priests and prophets continue through 7:3, followed by a WLC-family pe and the answering word at 7:4.
route.rationale: Date, delegation, destination, and the quoted fifth-month question form the complete inquiry to which the following word-events respond.
route.counterevidence: The question cannot be answered within this unit, so it requires the 7:1-8:23 response parent even though inquiry form and paragraph closure support separate retrieval.

route.title: Fasting-motive questions and former-prophet reminder
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The word-event at 7:4 directly answers the inquiry through questions about the object of fasting and feasting, then points back to former-prophet words; a WLC-family pe follows 7:7 before another word-event.
route.rationale: The double motive question and the reminder of earlier proclamation expose the inquiry's misplaced focus as one compact first response.
route.counterevidence: Verse 7 gestures to content supplied in 7:8-10, so it can bridge forward, but the renewed word-event and paragraph marker at 7:8 support the present close.

route.title: Justice command, ancestral refusal, and desolation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The renewed word-event at 7:8 introduces justice, kindness, and non-oppression commands; hardened refusal, wrath, call-response reversal, scattering, and land desolation continue to the pe after 7:14.
route.rationale: Command, rejection, judgment logic, and resulting desolation form a complete former-generation explanation rather than independent ethical sayings and history fragments.
route.counterevidence: The change from direct command to narrated refusal at 7:11 is a true rhetorical phase, but separating it would remove the conduct from the refusal it diagnoses.

route.title: Zion return and restored-city tableau
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A word-event at 8:1 opens repeated Yahweh-of-Armies sayings that move from jealousy and return to aged residents, playing children, the remnant's wonder, east-west rescue, and reciprocal people-God language through 8:8.
route.rationale: The short sayings build one restoration tableau: divine return makes ordinary intergenerational city life possible and culminates in gathered people dwelling in truth and righteousness.
rejected_alternatives: Zech.8.1-Zech.8.3 plus Zech.8.4-Zech.8.5 plus Zech.8.6-Zech.8.6 plus Zech.8.7-Zech.8.8
route.counterevidence: WLC-family marks after 8:3, 8:5, and 8:6 confirm recoverable sub-sayings, but surface microchunks would replace a cumulative tableau with formula-sized fragments.

route.title: Strengthened hands and curse-to-blessing reversal
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The repeated saying and Let your hands be strong at 8:9 begin an exhortation keyed to the temple-foundation day; former wage-less conflict contrasts with present seed peace, inheritance, and curse-to-blessing reversal, ending with the repeated strengthening command and samekh after 8:13.
route.rationale: The opening and closing hand-strength refrains frame the former-versus-now reversal as one exhortation, with agricultural and social outcomes functioning inside it.
route.counterevidence: The causal formula at 8:14 explains why the new good will persist and therefore links forward, but it also restarts a distinct intention-and-conduct movement.

route.title: Renewed purpose for good and truth-peace conduct
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: For Yahweh of Armies says at 8:14 restarts with a past judgment versus present good-intention comparison; do-not-fear and These are the things commands specify truthful speech, peaceful judgment, nonmalice, and rejection of false oath through 8:17 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: The renewed intention grounds the conduct list, so promise and imperatives remain together as one rationale-and-response oracle.
route.counterevidence: The unit continues the reversal announced at 8:13, making 8:9-17 a strong larger alternative, but 8:14's causal restart and 8:17 closure support a child surface with mandatory parent hydration.

route.title: Fasts transformed into joyful feasts
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A renewed word-event at 8:18 introduces the fourth-, fifth-, seventh-, and tenth-month fast register; their reversal into joy and feasts and the therefore command to love truth and peace conclude at the pe after 8:19.
route.rationale: The enumerated fasts receive one shared reversal and ethical close, directly answering the original inquiry without needing the following nations tableau to complete its syntax.
route.counterevidence: Verse 19 is highly retrievable as the explicit answer, but separating it from its word-event heading would create a contextless calendar pronouncement.

route.title: Cities and nations seek Yahweh
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: A fresh Yahweh-of-Armies saying at 8:20 opens with intercity dialogue and expands to many peoples and strong nations; the ten-men skirt image at 8:23 intensifies and closes the nations-seeking movement.
route.rationale: The movement grows from one city's invitation to multinational pilgrimage and a final direct-speech explanation, forming one expanding tableau.
route.counterevidence: A WLC-family samekh after 8:22 marks the final image as a distinct saying, but it functions as the climax rather than a disconnected unit.

route.title: Geographic burden and protected house
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The burden heading at 9:1 begins a place-by-place movement from Hadrach and Damascus through coastal cities; judgment, remnant incorporation, and Yahweh's encampment around the house resolve at 9:8 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: The geographic chain is governed by one advancing oracle whose outcomes culminate in protected-house closure rather than eight independent city sayings.
route.counterevidence: The burden heading has a framing function and the coastal sequence turns at 9:5, but neither heading nor city list is independently complete.

route.title: Zion royal acclamation and peace dominion
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Rejoice and Shout vocatives at 9:9 initiate a new acclamation; the arriving king image develops into removal of war instruments, speech of peace, and sea-to-sea dominion through 9:10 before direct address shifts at 9:11.
route.rationale: Arrival and dominion are parallel halves of one royal proclamation; isolating the famous arrival line would sever it from the peace and disarmament that define the movement's scope.
route.counterevidence: The As for you also transition at 9:11 creates a real child seam, while later Gospel reuse and royal-identity readings have no boundary authority.

route.title: Covenant prisoners, battle imagery, and flock restoration
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: As for you also at 9:11 shifts to direct covenant-prisoner address; return and double restoration lead into Judah-Ephraim weapon imagery, divine appearance and defense, flock salvation, crown jewels, and the goodness-and-abundance close at 9:17.
route.rationale: The prisoners' restoration expands into defended people and flock imagery, with 9:16-17 supplying the saving and flourishing resolution to the combat sequence.
route.counterevidence: The connective also and sustained second-person address can join 9:11 back to the acclamation, and the 9:9-17 parent is mandatory; nevertheless the address and action reset after 9:10 support the child seam.

route.title: Rain petition and false-guide indictment
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The imperative Ask Yahweh for spring rain at 10:1 is followed by a For-clause contrasting divine provision with teraphim, diviners, false dreams, and vain comfort; the shepherdless-flock result closes before the new anger declaration at 10:3 and a WLC-family pe follows 10:2.
route.rationale: True petition and counterfeit guidance form an antithetical wisdom-oracle movement whose practical result is a scattered, oppressed flock.
route.counterevidence: The rain imperative can stand as a concise exhortation, but its contrast and rationale are supplied by 10:2 and should not be detached.

route.title: Punished shepherds and strengthened battle flock
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: My anger at 10:3 resets the subject to shepherd judgment and divine visitation of Judah as a majestic battle horse; cornerstone, peg, bow, rulers, and victorious fighters continue through 10:5.
route.rationale: The judgment on failed leaders and transformation of the flock into a cohesive fighting force are one cause-and-result oracle before first-person house-restoration promises begin at 10:6.
route.counterevidence: The from-him catalogue in 10:4 is a recognizable subform, but it supplies leadership and equipment within the visited-flock movement rather than a separate list unit.

route.title: Strengthening, gathering, return, and restored walking
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: I will strengthen the house of Judah at 10:6 starts a sustained first-person restoration sequence; mercy, rejoicing, signaling, gathering, far-country remembrance, return from Egypt and Assyria, sea passage, humbled powers, and walking in Yahweh's name reach closure at 10:12 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: The repeated I-will promises trace one gathering-and-return arc whose final strengthening and walking statement resolves the movement.
route.counterevidence: The geographic return at 10:9 and exodus-like passage at 10:11 are recoverable phases, but splitting them would sever dispersion, gathering, return, and restored life.

route.title: Lebanon forest and shepherd lament
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Open your doors at 11:1 initiates a poetic imperative; tree and forest wails expand to shepherd lament and lion roar, ending at 11:3 with a WLC-family samekh before the prose command at 11:4.
route.rationale: The cascading cries over cedars, oaks, shepherd glory, and Jordan pride form one lament whose soundscape and imagery close before enactment begins.
route.counterevidence: The shepherd wail anticipates the following shepherd enactment and therefore links conceptually, but form, voice, and paragraph closure distinguish lament from sign-act.

route.title: Flock-of-slaughter and two-staff shepherd enactment
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The command Feed the flock of slaughter at 11:4 opens an enacted report; the narrator takes Favor and Union, rejects continued feeding, breaks Favor, receives and throws wages, and breaks Union through 11:14 and its paragraph mark.
route.rationale: Both named staffs and the wage episode are sequential actions inside one commissioned shepherd performance; the second staff's breaking supplies the sign-act's final enacted result.
route.counterevidence: The wage dialogue at 11:12 and renewed command at 11:13 are striking internal turns, and potter or treasury wording remains text-sensitive, but separating them would turn one enacted evaluation into a proof-text fragment.

route.title: Foolish shepherd enactment and woe
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Take again at 11:15 explicitly commissions a second shepherd role; the neglect-and-consumption catalogue at 11:16 leads to the woe and bodily judgment at 11:17, followed by paragraph closure.
route.rationale: Command, characterization through failed shepherd duties, and final woe form a complete second enactment contrasted with the first.
route.counterevidence: A WLC-family samekh follows 11:16 before the woe, but the woe directly judges the shepherd just portrayed and is required for closure.

route.title: Burden of siege, Judah's strength, and Jerusalem's defense
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The burden heading and creator preamble at 12:1 introduce cup and stone siege images; repeated in-that-day actions move through terror, Judah's confession, fiery chieftains, tents saved first, defended inhabitants, and the stated destruction of attacking nations at 12:9.
route.rationale: The siege tableau advances from threat to coordinated Judah-Jerusalem defense and closes with the purpose to destroy attackers before the spirit-and-mourning movement at 12:10.
route.counterevidence: A WLC-family pe after 12:6 and the save-Judah-first turn at 12:7 support an internal seam, but 12:7-9 completes the same siege-defense arc rather than opening a new form.

route.title: Spirit of supplication, household mourning, and cleansing fountain
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The spirit-pouring statement at 12:10 changes action from military defense to supplication and mourning; only-son grief expands through public and household laments, and the repeated in-that-day formula at 13:1 opens a fountain for the same named community.
route.rationale: Grace and supplication generate a widening lament whose sin-and-uncleanness fountain gives the sequence a cleansing resolution; the cross-chapter span protects both the lament and its outcome.
route.counterevidence: The WLC-family samekh after 12:14, chapter boundary, and action shift from mourning to fountain strongly support a surface seam; conversely the same audience and repeated in-that-day frame support resolution rather than restart. Pronoun and pierced-one witnesses cannot decide the literary boundary.
route.hold_question: Should Zech.13.1 remain the cleansing resolution of the Zech.12.10-14 supplication-and-mourning sequence, or surface with Zech.13.2-6 as the opening of a purification movement? The first preserves cause-to-resolution and shared audience; the second follows paragraph, chapter, and action-reset evidence.

route.title: Removal of idols and deceptive prophecy
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: It will happen in that day at 13:2 initiates removal of idols, prophets, and impurity; family enforcement, prophetic shame, vocation denial, and the wounds dialogue continue to the samekh after 13:6 before the sword summons at 13:7.
route.rationale: The successive cases test the disappearance and disavowal of deceptive prophecy, ending in direct dialogue that completes the purification tableau.
route.counterevidence: The fountain at 13:1 gives a strong thematic frame for purification, while wound wording in 13:6 is text-sensitive; neither requires merging the new cut-off action at 13:2 backward or forward.

route.title: Struck shepherd, scattered flock, and refined remnant
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Awake sword at 13:7 begins a new poetic summons; striking and scattering lead to the two-parts and third-part register, refining, reciprocal calling, and covenant-style recognition through 13:9 and its paragraph close.
route.rationale: Shepherd striking, flock scattering, numerical survival, and refining are one consequence-and-restoration poem, not detachable prediction or arithmetic fragments.
route.counterevidence: The shift from singular shepherd to land-wide fractions is substantial, but the surviving third is the resolution of the scattering initiated by the sword command.

route.title: Day siege, divine battle, mountain cleavage, and arrival
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Behold a day of Yahweh at 14:1 opens siege and plunder; Yahweh then goes out to fight, the mountain is split, escape follows, and Yahweh's arrival with holy ones closes 14:5 before a fresh in-that-day cosmic-light statement.
route.rationale: Siege, intervention, landscape transformation, escape, and arrival form one escalating day-theophany movement.
route.counterevidence: Verse 14:5 has flee or stop and suffix pressure, and the arrival clause may bridge forward into transformed-day conditions; no preferred reading is needed to recognize the 14:6 form reset.

route.title: Unique day, living waters, kingship, and secure city
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: It will happen in that day at 14:6 resets to cosmic light conditions; unique-day illumination, living waters, universal kingship, land transformation, elevated city, dwelling, and no-curse security continue through 14:11 before This will be the plague at 14:12.
route.rationale: Cosmic, hydrological, royal, topographic, and urban changes are successive dimensions of one transformed-world and secure-city tableau.
route.counterevidence: The repeated in-that-day formula at 14:8 and city-specific turn at 14:10 expose internal movements, while obscure light or cold wording at 14:6 lowers confidence but does not force formula-sized units.

route.title: Plague, panic, spoil, and camp animals
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: This will be the plague at 14:12 starts a new judgment catalogue; bodily wasting, divinely sent panic, mutual violence, Judah's fight, gathered wealth, and extension to camp animals continue through 14:15.
route.rationale: The animal plague explicitly mirrors the human plague, completing a single defeat-and-spoil movement before survivor pilgrimage begins at 14:16.
route.counterevidence: The spoil report at 14:14 is a result rather than a plague symptom, but it belongs to the same defeated-camp outcome and is enclosed by plague descriptions.

route.title: Survivor pilgrimage and withheld-rain cases
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Everyone left at 14:16 turns from defeated armies to annual pilgrimage; universal worship and Booths observance are tested by nonattendance, Egypt's case, plague or rain consequence, and the summary punishment at 14:19.
route.rationale: The general rule, family exception, Egypt example, and concluding sanction form one legal-casuistic pilgrimage movement.
route.counterevidence: The rain or plague ellipsis at 14:18 is text-sensitive and the Egypt case could be a dependent subcase, but neither supports detaching it from the rule it applies.

route.title: Holy bells, pots, and house coda
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: In that day at 14:20 begins a holiness inscription and vessel tableau; horse bells, temple pots, every Jerusalem and Judah pot, sacrificial use, and the final exclusion statement close the book at 14:21.
route.rationale: The coda extends holiness from cultic equipment to ordinary vessels and finishes with a house-of-Yahweh closure; both verses are needed for the expansion and endpoint.
route.counterevidence: The Canaanite or merchant rendering at 14:21 is text-sensitive, but no choice among renderings is required to identify the final holiness-and-house closure.

red_team_hard_seams.assessment: The doubled escape imperative changes form after the measuring interpretation; mandatory parent hydration preserves the indwelling bridge.
One courtroom scene remains open across cleansing, charge, and sign interpretation.
Embedded words interpret a still-open tableau and the olive questions resume afterward.
Dated inquiry, renewed word-events, rhetorical function, and paragraph closures support dependent children under the inquiry-response parent.
Direct-address and action reset at 9:11 supports children, with the whole parent mandatory.
Lament, first commanded enactment, and second command are distinct forms; both staffs remain within the first enactment.
Cause-to-cleansing resolution supports the cross-chapter unit, while paragraph, chapter, and action reset create the sole genuine hold question.
Action resets rather than formula counting support five movements, all hydrated to the full day-oracle parent.

genuine_hold_questions.question: Should Zech.13.1 remain the cleansing resolution of the Zech.12.10-14 supplication-and-mourning sequence, or surface with Zech.13.2-6 as the opening of a purification movement? The first preserves cause-to-resolution and shared audience; the second follows paragraph, chapter, and action-reset evidence.

source_limitations: WEB 1:18-21 corresponds to MT/WLC 2:1-4, and WEB 2:1-13 corresponds to MT/WLC 2:5-17; the crosswalk is evidence only.
OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family views and are not independent textual votes.

No preferred reading or translation was selected for speaker, pronoun, numeral, eye or iniquity, names, crown, royal, shepherd, wages, potter or treasury, pierced-one, wound, flee or stop, light, rain or plague, or Canaanite or merchant difficulties.
No passage-pinned primary LXX, DSS, Targum, rabbinic, ANE, Persian-period, or Second-Temple packet was available in the authorized input set; the gap is recorded rather than inferred.
